name: Sunday Night Static Live!
notes: The 7th edition of BDW's own weekly Sunday Night Static broadcast, aired the Sunday after BDW's own first pay-per-view, “The Return I.”

appearances.note: Billed for a Hardcore Championship defense against Arik Caine; Caine refused to wrestle and the match never happened.

matches.stipulation: Singles Match — #1 Contender for the Broken Championship
Over-the-Top Battle Royal — the winner becomes a BDW co-owner

eliminations.note: Final elimination; Jarone wins and is named BDW's third co-owner.

matches.note: Methid's own elimination point is never staged directly in the served text — the last the script shows of him is being clotheslined by JJ Jarone.

Billed as "Non-Title Match If Emilio Can Win He gets a World Title Shot." Called off by Co-Owner Jeffery before a bell ever rang, after Emilio Dervante attacked champion Sean McClancy pre-match and both men pursued McClancy's own manager Annie; Jeffery rebooked it as a ladder match for the World Heavyweight Championship at Anger & Rage (27 June 2004), banning Annie from ringside.
Main event; Broken Championship defense. Brock RockHard retains by submission, a kneeling Dragon Sleeper.

name: The Return I

date.source: BDW's own card for the show ("May 30th, 2004!") and its own title-history ledger ("On May 30, 2004"); the fed's own news of 1 June 2004 says the show aired late after technical difficulties.

notes: BDW's own first pay-per-view. Before the first match Co-Owner Jeffery fired Adam White, Julio Faustus and Judas Romonov on camera, and Apocalypse withdrew from the Hardcore match and bid the federation farewell, so a Hardcore match billed for nine went ahead with five.

appearances.note: Named in the Hardcore match's own nine-man billing on this page; fired on camera by Co-Owner Jeffery before the match.
Named in the Hardcore match's own nine-man billing on this page; fired on camera by Co-Owner Jeffery before the match.

matches.stipulation: Hardcore Title Match — Hardcore Elimination Match

eliminations.note: Pinned on the outside after a spinning heel kick; the page announces his elimination together with Flawless's.
Pinned down with Bruce's 2x4 after Andrew Irving's schoolboy.
Final fall, after Co-Owner Jeffery's chair shot missed Caine and nearly took Irving's head off; Arik Caine is the new Hardcore Champion.

matches.note: The match header on the page names six; Apocalypse came out and withdrew before the bell, and the commentary's own nine-man billing also names Adam White, Julio Faustus and Judas Romonov, all three fired by Co-Owner Jeffery earlier in the show.

Brock Rockhard pins Rob Zone with a set-up inverted DDT to become the new Broken Champion. Methid (flattened by Rob Zone's End Zone on the ramp) and Pretty Boy Evans (clotheslined by Methid on the ramp) never reach the ring; Jeremy Page is pushed off the top rope into the security barrier.

Sean McClancy pins Emilio Dervante after knocking him down with the title belt, with referee Brian Lasiner already downed by a chair; JJ Jarone had been powerbombed through the announce table. McClancy becomes BreakDown Wrestling's new World Champion.

name: Sunday Night Static (5th)

date.source: The fed's own news dates this broadcast "May 16, 2004" (topstory.php?id=9).

evidence.note: BDW's own news recap: the World Heavyweight Championship tournament's first round completed — "Pretty Boy Evans and JJ Jarone finaly get to meet eachother in the ring, did Evans tear Jarone apart like he said he could?" and "The Rebel took on Jackson Kable in what is said to be one of the greatest performances in a long time" — plus "Brock Rockhard makes his debut targeting 'The One' Jeremy Page."
The following week's card announcement confirms the round-1 winners advancing to round 2: JJ Jarone and Jackson Kable.
Roleplay #11 (25 May 2004), Brock RockHard's own pre-match promo against Jeremy Page, referencing the debut match already announced for this show.

Roleplay #12 (27 May 2004), Brock RockHard's own retrospective confirms he beat Jeremy Page in a finish his own father's-friend Bill ties to Co-Owner Jeffery's own booking ("you won that match because the owner seems to have some beef with Mr. Page").

notes: No dedicated results page survives; results reconstructed here (Jackson Kable defeated The Rebel; JJ Jarone defeated Pretty Boy Evans; Brock RockHard defeated Jeremy Page in a disputed finish) are secondary, from the fed's own news recap and roleplay corroboration, not a primary results document. The 6th Static's own results page (23 May 2004, /promotions/bdw/archive/sunday-night-static-6-2004-05-23.html) stages Brock RockHard's win over Jeremy Page, with Co-Owner Jeffery's chair, on that show; the 5th Static's own news recap says only that RockHard debuted "targeting" Page, so the two readings are kept side by side.

name: Sunday Night Static (6th)

date.source: BDW's own card announcement (topstory.php?id=10) books this show for "Sunday May 23rd"; the fed's own news of 25 May 2004 says it aired late, on the Monday night.

notes: The World Heavyweight Championship tournament's second round. The results page itself carries no date or show number; it is this show by its own tournament matches, the Return I hype that opens it, and the fed's own news of 25 May 2004.

matches.note: Andrew Irving wins with The Irvingizer, a moonsault off the top rope.

matches.stipulation: Four Way Over the Top Battle Royal — Broken Championship #1 Contendership

eliminations.note: Dropkicked off the top rope; Methid wins.

matches.note: The page bills the first entrant as "Julio"; the fed's own roster of the time carries one Julio, Julio Faustus, who is billed by his full name on the next week's pay-per-view card.
Co-Owner Jeffery climbs in from the crowd with the referee down and cracks a chair over Jeremy Page's skull; Brock Rockhard picks up the win.
After the match Co-Owner Jeffery gives UnderGround King his pink slip and punches him outside the arena.
The page declares a draw. At The Return I a week later Arik Caine complains that JJ Jarone was given the World title shot out of it while he was booked into the Hardcore match.

matches.stipulation: World Title Tournament Match 2nd Round — Main Event

date.source: Co-Owner Jeffery's own on-air booking, BDW's 7th Static (6 Jun 2004): "in two weeks on June 27th, at Anger & Rage."

evidence.note: Co-Owner Jeffery's own on-air announcement: "in two weeks on June 27th, at Anger & Rage, Sean McClancy will defend his title against, EMILIO DERVANTE!" as a ladder match, with McClancy's manager Annie banned from ringside — no results page for the show survives, and the outcome doesn't appear anywhere else in the held record.
